description: The big tree of the floodplain: 15-30 m tall with a stout, deeply furrowed grey trunk, a few heavy spreading limbs and a broad crown of glossy triangular leaves that flutter in the slightest wind. It grows on sandbars and banks where the water table is shallow, often leaning out over the channel, turns bright yellow in fall, and its cavities and dead limbs house woodpeckers, owls and wood ducks.

season_notes.winter: Bare: a pale grey crown of heavy limbs and stout twigs over the creek.
season_notes.spring: Red catkins in February-March, then fresh yellow-green leaves; in May the seeds drift down as cotton.
season_notes.summer: Glossy green crown that shimmers as the flat-stalked leaves flutter.
season_notes.fall: Bright yellow in November, the brightest colour on the creek, then bare.

notes: Fremont cottonwood is the floodplain giant of California's lowland and foothill streams, 12-35 m, here 15-24 m in the file with a veteran class to 30 m. Fast-growing and short-lived (100-150 years). A stout trunk (dbh 1-1.5 m on old trees: radius_ratio 0.05) with a short bole (0.15-0.25 of the height in the photos) that forks low into two to four massive, sinuous, spreading limbs (split_prob 0.6, decurrent crown: trunk.length_ratio 0.36 and long level-1 limbs). Rauh's model. The crown is broad and rounded in big lobes (photo W/H 1.0-1.5 for open-grown mature trees, 0.8-0.9 for younger ones; target 1.05), often asymmetric and leaning out over the water (lean_deg 12, asymmetry 0.2). Dead limbs commonly stand out of a living crown (deadwood, more in the veteran class) and snags are common. Bark pale on young stems, grey-brown and deeply furrowed on old trunks. Leaves 5-10 cm, broadly triangular (deltoid) with coarse rounded teeth, glossy on both faces, on long flattened stalks that make them flutter: leaf_shape deltoid (added to treegen.js for this species) with a glossy glint, light and dark leaf tints for the speckled look in the photos. Wind is not animated, so the flutter is not drawn. Deciduous: red catkins in February-March (not drawn), yellow-green leaves in March, glossy green all summer (photo linear r/g 0.83, b/g 0.51), bright yellow in November (r/g 1.4) and bare December-February.
